newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wellesley Club sells historic Wellington building.
newsitem.headline: Wellesley Club sells historic Wellington building.

text.p: The Timber Industry Federation said on Thursday it had bought the Wellesley Club building on Wellington's Maginnity St.

The financially troubled club closed in April while its members considered two options, whether to wind up the club or sell the building, understood to be worth about $1.5 million, The Evening Post reported.
The club was bought by Thorndon Group, the federation's trading and investment company. No purchase price was disclosed.
As part of the sale, the Wellesley Club will continue to use the building's facilities and keep all its chattels. The Thorndon Group will manage the club.
The club's membership is understood to have fallen from 400 last year to about 250 this year.
Wellesley Club chairman Tim Blundell said the club now faced an exciting future with the injection of funds and strong professional management.
Timber Industry Federation executive director Wayne Coffey said the intention was to restore the Wellesley building.
Coffey said he wanted to work closely with the Wellington City Council to ensure the club played a positive role in Wellington's downtown development.
The building is graded category one by the Historic Places Trust and is regarded as one of the best examples of Georgian architecture in New Zealand.
